title: Sharp CATE Curve Sets under Informative Dropout with Monotone Lipschitz Residuals
banked_reason: The promised ADJUVANT subgroup-sign reanalysis is not delivered; the available data do not supply the predeclared score, honest nuisance bands, fixed eligible-leaf protocol, or externally calibrated sensitivity value required for a faithful analysis.
gap_reasons: The promised ADJUVANT subgroup-sign reanalysis is not delivered: this theorem supplies only a generic construction and expressly leaves all trial-specific inputs and sign conclusions absent, so the applied deliverable was substituted by a conditional caveat.

The note proves an exact law-sharp curve identified set, exact pointwise projections, a strict-contraction characterization, and certified grid/flow representations, which is sufficient for the field tier. Its inference result is substantially narrower: uniform validity is conditional on an externally supplied band certificate, with no theorem establishing that the certified subclass is nonempty or constructing the band from the stated primitive Hölder model.

The proposed ADJUVANT subgroup-sign reanalysis is not delivered, leaving the package without the empirical evidence invoked to motivate its practical significance and limiting its leading-journal score.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a law-sharp monotone–Lipschitz CATE-curve set, exact obstacle-envelope projections and strictness, changing-contact stability, certified grid/flow representations, and a Wang-compatible endpoint-box comparison. The field package collapsed because its promised ADJUVANT sign reanalysis could not be run faithfully without a predeclared score, honest nuisance bands, a fixed eligible-leaf protocol, and externally calibrated L; the robust inference result also remained conditional on an external band certificate. The population identification and obstacle machinery remain reusable, but a future empirical run must freeze those inputs before outcome analysis rather than retroactively weakening the promise.
tldr: Informative dropout leaves an unknown residual restricted-survival contribution along the predeclared prognostic score. The greatest feasible monotone \(L\)-Lipschitz residual below a capacity \(u\) is the explicit envelope \(\Gamma_Lu\), which gives the exact pointwise projection of the law-sharp compact CATE-curve set. Joint curve coupling is nontrivial: the maintained set is strictly smaller than the Wang endpoint-selection box exactly when some arm-profile dropout capacity is nonzero. Support values separate into certified path-flow obstacle programs, and eroded grids have a uniform Hausdorff remainder even at zero-capacity contacts. For inference, a direct positive-part stability argument turns an externally certified nuisance band into an observable clipped compact convex whole-set superset with directed excess \(8r_n+2(Lh_n+Mh_n^\beta)\), without face differentiation or a direction net. Combining the density band with a finite-multinomial profile-mass region gives conservative simultaneous intervals for every eligible leaf and arbitrary post-selection validity. Efficient local-mass \((np_{\min,n})^{-1/2}\) calibration remains open because the declared score assumptions contain no score-to-statistic expansion or multiplier coupling.
gap: Wang et al. identify only covariatewise endpoint bounds and report adaptively favorable ADJUVANT leaves. Random-set, shape-restricted, optimized-value, and subgroup-inference papers each supply one ingredient but do not solve joint curve sharpness with estimated dropout obstacles or prove attainability of the continuous endpoint image as a distinct compatible-law class.
fill: Separate completion lemmas settle identification for the maintained monotone-Lipschitz class and the residual-continuity-only Wang benchmark; the support and eroded-grid theorems settle computation and approximation. On the externally certified subclass \(\mathfrak P_n^{\mathrm{band}}(r_n)\), the open critical-cone construction targets uniform whole-set and finite-VC leaf coverage with the uncompressed external-band, direction-net, and sampling errors displayed separately; post-selection inclusion is only a corollary.
